title: Reduction in saturated fat intake for cardiovascular disease
authors: Hooper L, Martin N, Jimoh OF, Kirk C, Foster E, Abdelhamid AS
population: 15 randomised trials (16 comparisons) aiming to reduce saturated fat intake, in adults with or without cardiovascular disease
funder: Internal sources: University of East Anglia; University of Manchester. External sources: studentship, Systematic Reviews Training Unit, Institute of Child Health, University of London; the World Health Organization funded the most recent update.
authorConflicts: Lee Hooper is a member of the WHO Nutrition Guidance Expert Advisory Group; WHO funded her institution for this update. No other conflicts declared.
result: Reducing saturated fat: combined cardiovascular events RR 0.83 (95% CI 0.70 to 0.98; 12 trials, 53,758 participants); number needed to treat 56 over about four years in primary prevention and 53 in secondary prevention; all-cause mortality RR 0.96 (0.90 to 1.03). Subgroup replacing saturated fat with polyunsaturated fat: cardiovascular events RR 0.79 (0.62 to 1.00; 8 trials, 4353 participants); all-cause mortality RR 0.96 (0.82 to 1.13; 7 trials, 4238 participants). The Minnesota Coronary trial was excluded because mean follow-up was about one year.
